LEARNING PATH LESSON · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Pause, Breathe Deeply, Think & Choose Kindness — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the single most valuable move in the whole class: the pause that fits between a feeling and a reaction, in four steps a four-year-old can run.

What is this?

Pause, breathe deeply, think and choose kindness are the four steps of the pause: freeze the moment, slow the body, see what is happening and then — the best part — choose what happens next.

What does it mean?

Between the spark and the flame there is a gap. Self-regulation is nothing more mysterious than a gap wide enough to choose in — and this card widens it with two words (pause, breathe) and two moves (think, choose).

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three ideas: the pause is a FREEZE (everything stops, including words); the breath is the remote control (slow breath, slow body); and the last step is a real CHOICE — nobody makes you kind; you get to pick it.

Why this matters

Every calm-down tool in the class — the courage ladder, the count to ten, the reset — is a variation of this pause. Learn it here, at calm-home scale, and it will be there in the storm.

What it teaches

Self-regulation (the executive-function showpiece), impulse control, metacognition (thinking about what is happening), and moral agency — the child as the chooser of their own next move.

Words to learn

pausebreathe deeplythinkchoosekindnessfreezegap

Say this to your child

“"Here is the strongest four-step move I know. One: PAUSE — everything stops, like a statue, even the angry words. Two: breathe deeply — in through the nose, out slow, and your body hears it and starts to settle. Three: think — what is actually happening? (He did not mean it. The game broke. I am tired.) Four — and this is the magic: CHOOSE. Nobody makes you yell and nobody makes you kind. You choose. And when you choose kindness, you are the strongest person in the room. The pause is where the power lives."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "This is the pause — the space where YOU choose."
  2. Run it small: someone says PAUSE — everyone freezes mid-motion (freeze dance style). Hold three seconds. Then one deep breath together: in through the nose, out slow.
  3. Add the think: "what is happening right now?" One sentence. Then the fourth step, spoken like a secret power: "and I choose kindness."
  4. Rehearse it on a pretend spark: "suppose your brother knocked your tower — PAUSE. Breathe. Think: he did not mean it. Choose: shall we build it again together?"
  5. Close with the freeze-dance game below and the takeaway: "the pause is yours; the choice is yours; the power is yours."

Look closer at the picture

On this card four panels run the sequence: Pause, a still boy with closed eyes; Breathe Deeply, a girl with a hand on her chest mid-breath; Think, a boy with a finger to his temple; and Choose Kindness, a girl hugging a pink heart — the whole gap between spark and choice, drawn in four frames.

Ask your child

"What is step one — freeze or fix?" "What does the deep breath do to the body?" "Who chooses the last step?" "What did YOU choose recently?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "Pause means everything stops!" "I choose kindness" (wield it gently when they do) or the honest one: "I forgot to pause and then I remembered."

Out in the real world

Real sparks arrive hourly: the knocked tower, the taken crayon, the wrong cup, the end of screen time. Run the pause at each one — often silently, hand on chest as the signal — and the gap becomes a habit their body knows even when their feelings are loud.

Try it together

Freeze-Dance with a Choice: music dances, then stops — PAUSE! Everyone freezes; one deep breath together; the leader asks "how do we choose to play the next round?" and offers two kind options (gentle hands? new game? swap partners?). The children pick — the choosing is the lesson, dressed as a dance game. Rotate the leader every round.

Understanding check

Ask: "What stops first? What does the slow breath do? Who makes the last choice?" Pause, settles the body, me — three answers and the pause belongs to your child.

Parent tips

Practise the pause on calm days, never in the storm — the drill must live somewhere safe before it can work somewhere hard. And use the silent signal (hand on your own chest) instead of shouting PAUSE at a boiling child: the gesture says we do this together, which is the only version that teaches.

This lesson pairs with the Pause, Breathe Deeply, Think & Choose Kindness flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Feelings & Kindness (Class 38).
